articles.title: Colombian president ends university autonomy policy, granting police access to campuses
articles.author: BreakThrough News
articles.content_excerpt: A little over a month into his term, far-right President Abelardo de la Espriella continues to advance a security agenda that often conflicts with certain rights historically won by Colombians. This time, De la Espriella has signed a decree allowing police access to university campuses. In several Latin American countries, the prohibition of police access to universities has been established through student struggle to prevent abuses by authorities against student movements. Thus, universities have historically become places where students seek refuge from repression, arrest, and regroup during times of intense social mobilization. articles.author: Ana Vračar
articles.content_excerpt: Leaders of pro-independence parties in Ireland, Scotland, and Wales met in Cardiff on Monday to sign a memorandum of understanding laying out a plan for strengthened cooperation. articles.author: Pablo Meriguet
articles.content_excerpt: Right-wing and far-right governments in Latin America have adopted a very similar discourse regarding insecurity.
